1) Background / Context

The project involves developing a sophisticated RSS Reader application using Rails 6. This application will provide a user-friendly interface for managing and reading RSS feeds, alongside offering a REST-like API for external clients. The system is set up to enhance users' ability to organize, manage, and share content seamlessly.

 2) Objectives

- To create an intuitive platform for reading and managing RSS feeds.
- To implement functionality for extracting full-text articles from partial-content feeds.
- To offer robust podcast support, remembering playback position.
- To facilitate actions on articles, such as starring or marking as read.
- To enable powerful search capabilities with a savable search syntax.
- To support various sharing services and read-it-later options.
- To ensure articles are updated if the original content changes.
- To integrate support for YouTube channels and playlists.
- To allow newsletters to be handled directly within the app.

 3) Stakeholders & Users

- End Users: Individuals utilizing the application to manage their RSS feeds, podcasts, and newsletters.
- Developers: Building and maintaining the system.
- Administrators: Managing subscriptions, user accounts, and system settings.
- Third-party Clients: Applications connecting through the provided API.

 4) Functional Descriptions

- Feed Management: Users can subscribe to, organize, and manage RSS feeds.
- Full-text Extraction: Provides complete article content even for feeds that only offer partial posts.
- Podcast Support: Users can listen to podcasts within the app with playback position saved.
- Automated Actions: Configure actions to automatically process articles (e.g., star, mark as read).
- Search Functionality: Users can perform complex searches and save frequent queries.
- Sharing and Saving: Configure sharing services for quick access to read-it-later options.
- Article Updates: Automatic update of articles if the original source changes, highlighting changes.
- YouTube and Newsletters: Follow YouTube channels and integrate newsletters into the app seamlessly.

 5) Non-Functional Descriptions

- Scalability: Handle large numbers of feeds and users efficiently.
- Security: Protect user data and interactions with secure authentication mechanisms.
- Usability: Ensure the app is user-friendly and accessible.
- Performance: Deliver quick load times and smooth transitions between content.
- Compatibility: Provide a robust API to support third-party applications and integrations.

-- Schema for database: schemabench_0071
CREATE TABLE `users` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `email` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `encrypted_password` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `name` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `created_at` datetime NOT NULL,
  `updated_at` datetime NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  UNIQUE KEY `index_users_on_email` (`email`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `feeds` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `title` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `url` varchar(1024) NOT NULL,
  `site_url` varchar(1024) DEFAULT NULL,
  `feed_type` varchar(50) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'rss',
  `language` varchar(20) DEFAULT NULL,
  `created_at` datetime NOT NULL,
  `updated_at` datetime NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  UNIQUE KEY `index_feeds_on_url` (`url`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `subscriptions` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `feed_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `folder` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `active` tinyint(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT '1',
  `created_at` datetime NOT NULL,
  `updated_at` datetime NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  UNIQUE KEY `index_subscriptions_on_user_id_and_feed_id` (`user_id`,`feed_id`),
  KEY `index_subscriptions_on_feed_id` (`feed_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `subscriptions_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `users` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `subscriptions_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`feed_id`) REFERENCES `feeds` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `articles` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `feed_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `guid` varchar(512) NOT NULL,
  `title` varchar(1024) NOT NULL,
  `url` varchar(1024) DEFAULT NULL,
  `author` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `content` longtext DEFAULT NULL,
  `summary` longtext DEFAULT NULL,
  `published_at` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `updated_at_source` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `is_full_content` tinyint(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `created_at` datetime NOT NULL,
  `updated_at` datetime NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  UNIQUE KEY `index_articles_on_feed_id_and_guid` (`feed_id`,`guid`),
  KEY `index_articles_on_feed_id` (`feed_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `articles_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`feed_id`) REFERENCES `feeds` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `article_states` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `article_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `starred` tinyint(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `read_at` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `saved_for_later` tinyint(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `created_at` datetime NOT NULL,
  `updated_at` datetime NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  UNIQUE KEY `index_article_states_on_user_id_and_article_id` (`user_id`,`article_id`),
  KEY `index_article_states_on_article_id` (`article_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `article_states_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `users` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `article_states_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`article_id`) REFERENCES `articles` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `podcast_playbacks` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `article_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `position_seconds` int(11) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `duration_seconds` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `completed` tinyint(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `last_played_at` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `created_at` datetime NOT NULL,
  `updated_at` datetime NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  UNIQUE KEY `index_podcast_playbacks_on_user_id_and_article_id` (`user_id`,`article_id`),
  KEY `index_podcast_playbacks_on_article_id` (`article_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `podcast_playbacks_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `users` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `podcast_playbacks_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`article_id`) REFERENCES `articles` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `search_queries` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `query` text NOT NULL,
  `created_at` datetime NOT NULL,
  `updated_at` datetime NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  UNIQUE KEY `index_search_queries_on_user_id_and_name` (`user_id`,`name`),
  CONSTRAINT `search_queries_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `users` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `sharing_services` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `service_name` varchar(100) NOT NULL,
  `service_type` varchar(50) NOT NULL,
  `config` text DEFAULT NULL,
  `enabled` tinyint(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT '1',
  `created_at` datetime NOT NULL,
  `updated_at` datetime NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `index_sharing_services_on_user_id` (`user_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `sharing_services_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `users` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `automation_rules` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `rule_type` varchar(50) NOT NULL,
  `conditions` text NOT NULL,
  `actions` text NOT NULL,
  `enabled` tinyint(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT '1',
  `created_at` datetime NOT NULL,
  `updated_at` datetime NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `index_automation_rules_on_user_id` (`user_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `automation_rules_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `users` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `api_clients` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `api_key` char(64) NOT NULL,
  `api_secret` char(64) NOT NULL,
  `last_used_at` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `created_at` datetime NOT NULL,
  `updated_at` datetime NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  UNIQUE KEY `index_api_clients_on_api_key` (`api_key`),
  KEY `index_api_clients_on_user_id` (`user_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `api_clients_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `users` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `newsletters` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `email_address` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `title` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `active` tinyint(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT '1',
  `created_at` datetime NOT NULL,
  `updated_at` datetime NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  UNIQUE KEY `index_newsletters_on_email_address` (`email_address`),
  KEY `index_newsletters_on_user_id` (`user_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `newsletters_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `users` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;
